q: 'No account with that email' vs 'Wrong password' messages allow …
why: Attackers learn which emails have accounts. Use one generic message.

q: Why hash a dummy password when the user does not exist?
o: So the response time is the same and doesn't reveal whether the account exists
why: A fast 'no such user' path leaks existence through timing.

q: Locking an account after 5 wrong passwords is a safe default.
why: Myth. Anyone can lock out a victim (a denial of service). Prefer layered, sliding-window rate limits per IP and per account.

q: Which should never appear in logs?
o: the time of a failed login
why: Passwords (even wrong ones) and tokens never go in logs.
